A content delivery network is a system that helps websites load quickly no matter where a visitor is located. Normally, every request for a webpage, image, or video travels all the way back to a single origin server — the original computer where that website's files are permanently stored. If that server is far away, loading takes longer because data must travel a great distance. A content delivery network solves this by placing many copies of the same files on servers scattered around the world, called edge locations, since they sit at the "edge" of the network, close to where people actually are. When someone requests a page, the network checks whether a nearby edge location already has a saved copy. If it does, that is called a cache hit, meaning the content is delivered instantly from a nearby copy instead of the distant original. Think of it like a chain of bakeries that all sell bread baked at one central factory; rather than shipping every loaf from the factory whenever someone wants bread, small local branches keep fresh loaves ready, so customers get bread quickly without waiting for a delivery from far away. Only when a nearby branch runs out does it need to fetch more from the factory. This arrangement reduces waiting time, lowers strain on the original server, and keeps websites working smoothly even during busy periods or heavy traffic, since load gets spread across many locations instead of one.

| Term | Plain meaning | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Origin server | The original computer storing a website's actual files | Every new or updated piece of content starts here |
| Edge location | A smaller, nearby server holding copies of popular content | Shortens the distance data has to travel to reach a visitor |
| Cache hit | When requested content is already saved at a nearby edge location | Content loads faster and the original server is not bothered |
| Cache miss | When the nearby copy is missing or outdated, so the request goes to the origin server | Explains why some loads are slower than others |
